sections.heading: Objectives of the Practice:
bullet_points: To encourage students, faculties and larger campus community to be conscious of environmental issues and to take responsibility for sustainable environment.
To include sustainable techniques in campus, incorporating green ideas into a significant operation.
To reduce water usage by implementing water conservation measures into practice, such as rainwater harvesting.
To create green garden with focus on herbal and medicinal plants..
To encourage clean and healthy campus environment by supporting the cleanliness drive and contributing to national cleaning initiatives.
To host sustainability seminars and workshops and educate campus on environmental sustainability.

sections.heading: The Context
paragraphs: Shree Devi Institute of Technology (SDIT) is situated in a semi-urban area surrounded by lush greenery in Mangalore, India. The institution emphasizes environmental conservation and sustainability, given its expansive green campus. The local community, a mix of urban and rural residents, enriches the region’s cultural and ecological diversity. SDIT leverages this setting to promote environmental awareness, implement sustainable initiatives and engage stakeholders in fostering environmental responsibility. Actively participating in the cleanliness drive by organizing awareness campaigns and initiatives to promote hygiene and sanitation on campus and in the surrounding community, the Institution prioritizes maintaining a clean and healthy environment for its students, faculty, staff and the society. Our college campus offers a unique blend of a litter-free environment and fresh air, creating an ideal setting for students to concentrate on their academic pursuits.

sections.heading: The Practice
paragraphs: At Shree Devi Institute of Technology (SDIT), cultivating a culture of environmental awareness and sustainability is paramount. Through a comprehensive approach, SDIT strives to instill environmental consciousness and responsibility among students, faculties, staff, and society.
bullet_points: Awareness Campaigns and Education: SDIT organizes campaigns, workshops, and events on environmental issues and sustainability, including street plays, slogan writing, talks on energy conservation, face painting, and celebrating Environmental Day. Activities like gifting saplings to guests instead of bouquets aim to enhance understanding and encourage proactive engagement in sustainability efforts.

Sustainable Campus Practices: The Institution has gone green, using LED lighting and solar water heaters to reduce emissions and has made a significant step towards sustainability with a 136-kW solar power system.

Water Conservation: Water conservation is a significant priority for SDIT. Rainwater collection reduces water consumption and encourages responsible water management, lowering dependency on limited resources and improving environmental sustainability.

Waste Management: Effective waste management is critical to a sustainable environment. An encouraging picture on the notice board encourages students to keep the area clean. Students dispose the E-waste in the allotted room, which promotes responsibility and keeps the area organized.

Green Gallery: SDIT has established a botanical garden featuring medicinal and herbal plants, serving as both an educational resource and a biodiversity sanctuary. SDIT campus is home to three remarkable green spaces: The Eco Trail, a scenic pathway promoting environmental awareness, the stunning Green Blossom fountain, and the Canteen Garden, also named Eco bite, building a bond with nature and a sense of community.

Cleanliness Drive: SDIT actively supports cleanliness drive. Through campus-wide cleanliness drives and awareness campaigns, the institution promotes a clean and healthy environment. Participation in these national initiatives underscores SDIT’s dedication to ecological responsibility and community engagement.
Segregation of Wastes: SDIT has placed separate bins for dry and wet waste across the campus.
Sewage Treatment Plant: Waste water from toilets, sinks, and other sources is channelled through pipelines into an underground sewage system.
E-Waste: Additionally, an MOU with Moogambigai Metal Refineries, signed on January 21, 2021, ensures proper disposal of electronic waste. There is separate place to collect E-waste.

Vermicomposting: Included in their dedication to sustainability, students have launched a vermicomposting effort. Vermicomposting bins collect and treat organic waste, such as food leftovers and garden clippings. The resulting compost is utilized to fertilize plants, promoting a closed-loop waste management system.

sections.heading: The Practice
bullet_points: “Samarpan” is a comprehensive project at Shree Devi Institute of Technology (SDIT) that aims to significantly improve society via a range of outreach programs and activities. A wide range of activities are included in this effort, such as community involvement, healthcare awareness, environmental conservation, educational support and cultural preservation.

Annual Outreach Programs: Students organize yearly outreach programs such as visits to orphanages, old age homes, rural schools and other charitable institutions. Seminar halls are transformed into movie theaters, with proceeds donated to charitable trusts. Fairs and sales activities are also organized, with the generated funds directed towards donations.

Charity Initiatives: The campus transformed into a hub of charitable enthusiasm, with students selling products in public places, engaging in educational movie sessions, participating in enjoyable games and activities, showcasing their handicraft skills and savoring a food fest, all in support of the Samarpan charity initiative.

Collaboration: SDIT signed an MOU with Aloka Foundation, Mangalore, on September 17, 2021. The primary objective of this partnership is to provide essential resources such as food, medicine, and financial aid to the underprivileged community, addressing their immediate needs and improving their quality of life.

Digital Literacy Initiatives: An instructional kiosk booth was used as part of a computer awareness initiative for rural households, aimed at teaching children and seniors alike the value of technology.

Environmental Conservation: Regular beach cleaning drives involve students, faculty, and volunteers in litter removal. Participants are provided with gloves, bags, and cleaning materials, and waste is sorted for proper disposal. Cleanliness drives are also held in the campus and in surrounding areas, with suitable waste bins and signage urging responsible disposal.

Educational Programs: Regular training sessions are conducted in nearby schools to enhance digital literacy. Programs and events are also organized to raise awareness about AIDS and related issues, including educational sessions and campaigns on prevention and support for affected individuals.

Healthcare Initiatives: SDIT often hosts blood donation drives on campus in partnership with local blood banks. These programs provide a safe environment for students, staff, and community members to donate blood, with medical professionals present to ensure donor safety. Guest speakers discuss the necessity of blood donation.

Partnerships for Environmental Causes: SDIT partners with environmental organizations like Vana Charitable Trust, an NGO, to organize joint community cleaning drives. The institution also hosts talks, presentations, and tree plantation drives by experts on environmental conservation.

sections.heading: Evidence of success
bullet_points: Samarpan has achieved significant success through impactful events. A donation drive at St. Anthony’s Ashram provided essential resources such as home essentials, clothes and stationery, fulfilling the residents’ needs. Additionally, cultural programs uplifted the spirits of differently-abled individuals, fostering inclusion and happiness. A New Year’s celebration at White Doves Psychiatric Nursing and Destitute Home brought joy and vigor to the children.
At Anirveda, a school for special children, students spent quality time playing games and distributing sweets, creating a joyful atmosphere and enriching the lives of the children.

Samarpan raised awareness about AIDS through seminars and workshops. Fundraising events supported HIV positive children, demonstrating a strong commitment to social causes. From the outreach club we contributed to Samvedhana Home for Children and Snehadeep Orphanage.
The blood donation drives at SDIT have been highly successful, with numerous donors contributing blood, thereby potentially saving many lives.

The collaboration between SDIT and Aloka Foundation underscores a shared commitment to serving the underprivileged and promoting equity. Leveraging student involvement, this partnership has significantly improved the lives of marginalized individuals and enriched the educational experiences of SDIT students.

sections.heading: About the committee
paragraphs:
Karnataka Education Act, 1983, Section 2(29) states: “Ragging is defined as intimidating, inducing, compelling, or forcing a student to do any act that violates his person, diminishes his human dignity, or exposes him to ridicule or causes him to refrain from doing any lawful act, by using criminal force against him or by holding out to him any treat of such intimidation, wrongful restraint, wrongful confinement, injury, or the use of criminal force.”
Section 116: Ragging Penalties
Raiding is not permitted for anyone enrolled in an educational program, including one run directly by the university or the central government.
If found guilty of violating sub-section (1), the offender faces a maximum sentence of one year in prison, a maximum fine of two thousand rupees, or both.

sections.heading: The penalties that follow for ragging have been established by the University Grants Commission’s institutional regulations.
paragraphs: The potential penalties for individuals found guilty of ragging at the institutional level may include any one or all of the following,
bullet_points: Depending on the type and seriousness of the offense as determined by the institution’s Anti-Ragging Committee.
Suspension from classes and from using academic resources. removing or not awarding a fellowship, scholarship, or other advantages.
Declining to participate in any assessment process, examination, or test. withholding results.
Declining to represent the organization in any youth festival, competition, meet, regional, national, or worldwide.
Removal or suspension from the hostel.
Exclusion from the organization and, as a result, a temporary ban from entry to any other organization.
A fine that could be anywhere from Rs 25,000 to Rs 1 lakh.
Collective Punishment: The institution may use collective punishment if the individuals who are perpetrating or encouraging the crime of ragging are not found.

sections.heading: Grievance Redressal
paragraphs:
The wellbeing of our students is our top priority at SDIT. Our thoughtfully developed 4-step redressal process enables us to promptly and successfully handle student complaints.
Students can file complaints with the student welfare officer for solve concerning non-academic matters, such as any incidents of ragging or issues, scholarships, and cultural and sporting events.

sections.heading: Step 1: Complaining in writing
paragraphs: It is mandatory for students to complete the Student Grievance Form and send it to the Director of Student Affairs either by handwritten letter or email. The department’s Proctor must also receive a copy of the complaint.
In their complaint, students must make sure to provide all of their credentials (name, course, year, etc.).

sections.heading: Step 2: Confirmation
paragraphs: The Directorate of Student Affairs will document and confirm the complaint upon receipt.

sections.heading: Step 3: Take Initiative
paragraphs: Following the complaint’s verification, the Department investigates the matter and takes the required action to fix the problem.

sections.heading: Step 4: Notifying the student
paragraphs: The student is informed of the resolution and the complaint once it has been addressed.

Section 116: Ragging Penalties

Raiding is not permitted for anyone enrolled in an educational program, including one run directly by the university or the central government.

If found guilty of violating sub-section (1), the offender faces a maximum sentence of one year in prison, a maximum fine of two thousand rupees, or both.

## The penalties that follow for ragging have been established by the University Grants Commission’s institutional regulations.

The potential penalties for individuals found guilty of ragging at the institutional level may include any one or all of the following,

- Depending on the type and seriousness of the offense as determined by the institution’s Anti-Ragging Committee.

- Suspension from classes and from using academic resources. removing or not awarding a fellowship, scholarship, or other advantages.

- Declining to participate in any assessment process, examination, or test. withholding results.

- A fine that could be anywhere from Rs 25,000 to Rs 1 lakh.

- Collective Punishment: The institution may use collective punishment if the individuals who are perpetrating or encouraging the crime of ragging are not found.

## Objectives:

- Preventing it from happening by adhering to the legal requirements set forth in the regulations.

- Punishing individuals who engage in ragging in accordance with the applicable legal rules.

## Grievance Redressal

The wellbeing of our students is our top priority at SDIT. Our thoughtfully developed 4-step redressal process enables us to promptly and successfully handle student complaints.
Students can file complaints with the student welfare officer for solve concerning non-academic matters, such as any incidents of ragging or issues, scholarships, and cultural and sporting events.

## Step 1: Complaining in writing

It is mandatory for students to complete the Student Grievance Form and send it to the Director of Student Affairs either by handwritten letter or email. The department’s Proctor must also receive a copy of the complaint.

In their complaint, students must make sure to provide all of their credentials (name, course, year, etc.).

## Step 2: Confirmation

The Directorate of Student Affairs will document and confirm the complaint upon receipt.

## Step 3: Take Initiative

Following the complaint’s verification, the Department investigates the matter and takes the required action to fix the problem.

## Step 4: Notifying the student

The student is informed of the resolution and the complaint once it has been addressed.

## About the committee

Shree Devi Institute of Technology is dedicated to providing a respectful and deserving environment free from harassment and discrimination for both its staff and students. The purpose of the college’s Women Anti- Harassment Committee is to increase awareness of women’s issues and create a safe environment for female students. With the objective of promoting women’s intellectual and social advancement, the committee advocates for women’s empowerment via awareness campaigns, seminars, guest lectures, and other welfare initiatives.

## Structure

As chairperson, a female instructor is in charge. Representatives from department, including faculty and students, make up the group. The committee develops strategies to accomplish the goals during its recurring meetings.

## Objectives

- To encourage the equality and respect of women in society.

- To inform female employees and students of their legal rights

- To guarantee that, both inside the organization and in the community, sexual harassment is viewed as a criminal offense and an inappropriate social behavior.

## Roles and Responsibilities

- Going to educate people on the subject.

- Educating them about their ability to file a complaint against the criminal.

- Helping staff members and students know why they are at the college and emphasizing the value of their labor and study.

- Encouraging a variety of activities and exercises for the staff’ and students’ personal growth.

- Encouraging staff members and students to use the complaint committee.

- To provide the knowledge of self-defense.

sections.heading: Overview
paragraphs: Aeronautical Engineering encompasses designing aircraft, stability and control of aerospace vehicles, propulsion systems, low and high speed aerodynamics and also development of advanced technologies in the field of defense and space science.

Career opportunities are vast especially in the fields of designing and planning , building, testing ,operation and upkeep of both commercial and military aircraft, ballistic capsules and space vehicles and their components as well as satellites and missiles.

The department has some of the best and experienced faculty members to provide students with individual attention and advanced training. The department has adopted Project Based learning, where in students are encouraged to apply their creative problem solving knowledge to real world problems.

sections.heading: Program Outcomes (POs)
bullet_points: PO1: Engineering knowledge: Apply the knowledge of mathematics, science, engineering fundamentals, and an engineering specialization to the solution of complex engineering problems.

PO2: Problem analysis: Identify, formulate, review research literature, and analyze complex engineering problems reaching substantiated conclusions using first principles of mathematics, natural sciences, and engineering sciences.

PO3: Design/development of solutions: Design solutions for complex engineering problems and design system components or processes that meet the specified needs with appropriate consideration for the public health and safety, and the cultural, societal, and environmental considerations.

PO5: Modern tool usage: Create, select, and apply appropriate techniques, resources, and modern engineering and IT tools including prediction and modeling to complex engineering activities with an understanding of the limitations.

PO6: The engineer and society: Apply reasoning informed by the contextual knowledge to assess societal, health, safety, legal and cultural issues and the consequent responsibilities relevant to the professional engineering practice.

PO7: Environment and sustainability: Understand the impact of the professional engineering solutions in societal and environmental contexts, and demonstrate the knowledge of, and need for sustainable development.
PO8: Ethics: Apply ethical principles and commit to professional ethics and responsibilities and norms of the engineering practice.
PO9: Individual and team work: Function effectively as an individual, and as a member or leader in diverse teams, and in multidisciplinary settings.

PO10: Communication: Communicate effectively on complex engineering activities with the engineering community and with society at large, such as, being able to comprehend and write effective reports and design documentation, make effective presentations, and give and receive clear instructions.

PO11: Project management and finance: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the engineering and management principles and apply these to one’s own work, as a member and leader in a team, to manage projects and in multidisciplinary environments.
PO12: Life-long learning: Recognize the need for, and have the preparation and ability to engage in independent and life-long learning in the broadest context of technological change.

sections.heading: Eligibility
paragraphs: Pre-University Board or any other examinations recognized by the University or equivalent thereto, with a minimum of 45%* aggregate marks in Physics, Chemistry & Mathematics.

sections.heading: Note:
paragraphs: *40% for students belonging to SC/ST and OBC categories.

Independence Day Charity Event: The Independence Day Charity Event organized by the MCA department aims to celebrate the spirit of freedom while contributing to a noble cause. This event not only fosters a sense of social responsibility but also highlights the importance of giving back to the community in honor of India’s independence.

Social Out Reach Program:The Social Outreach Program organized by the MCA department includes a visit to a government school, where students actively engage with children to support their learning and development. During the visit, students conduct educational activities such as providing study materials, and share knowledge about technology. This initiative aims to foster social responsibility, inspire young minds, and bridge the educational gap in underprivileged communities.

Industrial Visits: from the college offers students practical exposure to real-world applications of their academic learning. It provides an opportunity to interact with industry professionals, understand operational processes, and explore the latest technologies in the field. Such visits help bridge the gap between theoretical knowledge and industry practices. Students gain insights that aid in career preparation and enhance their overall educational experience.

Medha: is a national level technical fest organized by the MCA department, which is aimed at promoting innovation, creativity, and technical skills amongst students. The event features various competitions across different domains of technology and engineering. It serves as a platform for students to enhance their skills like team management, communication, leadership and gain hands-on experience in event management. Medha fosters a spirit of collaboration and learning, bringing together participants from colleges across the country.

Outbound Training: for college students is an experiential learning program designed to develop essential skills like leadership, teamwork, and problem-solving. The training typically involves outdoor activities, adventure sports, and group challenges that encourage personal growth and effective communication. It helps students build resilience, confidence, and decision-making abilities. Such programs provide a dynamic environment for students to learn outside the traditional classroom setting.

Cyber Security Workshop: A Cyber Security Workshop conducted for MCA students to provide hands-on experience and in-depth knowledge of various cybersecurity practices, tools, and techniques. The workshop covers topics such as network security, ethical hacking, malware analysis, and data protection strategies, equipping students with the skills to protect against cyber threats. It also emphasizes the importance of staying updated with the latest security trends to ensure a secure digital environment in both personal and professional spheres.

IOT Workshop: An IoT Workshop is conducted for MCA students to understand the fundamental concepts and applications of the Internet of Things, focusing on connecting physical devices to the internet for smart data collection and automation. The workshop includes hands-on sessions on building IoT systems, using sensors, and implementing cloud-based solutions for real-time data analysis. Students gain practical insights into IoT protocols, security challenges, and emerging trends, preparing them for careers in this rapidly growing field.

It helps foster networking, mentorship, and knowledge sharing, enabling alumni to guide and inspire the next generation of professionals. The association also organizes events, reunions, and career development opportunities to strengthen the community and provide support for career growth and industry connections.

The workshop covers key features such as email marketing, social media integration, customer journey mapping, and data-driven decision-making. Students gain practical experience in leveraging Marketing Cloud to create personalized, effective campaigns, preparing them for roles in digital marketing and customer relationship management.

The event features a variety of cultural performances, games, and activities that bring students and faculty together, fostering a sense of unity and community. It serves as a fun and meaningful way to celebrate diversity while strengthening the bond within the department.

These activities include organizing workshops, technical talks, coding competitions, internships, and community service projects, helping students develop practical skills and contribute to societal development. ## About Master of Computer Applications (MCA)

The Master of Computer Applications (MCA) program at Shree Devi Institute of Technology is designed to equip students with advanced knowledge and skills in computer science, programming, and software development. A two year’s full-time course includes interactive classes, national seminars, outbound activities and emphasizes practical experience through projects and internships. Upon completion, graduates are prepared for careers in software development, IT consulting, and systems analysis.

It is the branch of engineering that involves the production and usage of heat and mechanical power for the design, production, and operation of machines and tools. It is one of the oldest, broadest and ever green engineering disciplines with a vast scope of employment globally.

The Department of Mechanical engineering at Shree Devi Institute of Technology is backed by well developed Laboratories such as CAED lab, CAMD lab with state of the art hardware and software for the students to enhance their creativity and talent. pages.full_content:
## Overview

Dynamic and inclusive clubs are designed to identify and nurture student talents in technical, cultural, co-curricular, and sports activities. With a long-term vision in mind, these clubs aims to provide a platform for students to explore their passions, develop their skills, and excel in their respective fields. Following clubs are functioning in the institution:

## Lingua Nova

A vibrant club dedicated to enhancing language proficiency and fostering essential corporate skills. Members engage in interactive sessions and workshops to improve their linguistic abilities, focusing on both verbal and written communication. The club also provides opportunities to develop skills such as public speaking, negotiation, and business correspondence, preparing members for professional success in a globalized world.

## Media Mavericks

This club is a hub for photography, videography, and media-related activities. Members explore the art and techniques of capturing images and videos, from mastering camera settings to editing software. They collaborate on creative projects, learn about industry trends, and gain hands-on experience in various media formats, making it an ideal platform for aspiring media professionals and enthusiasts alike.

## Coders Nexus

At Coders Nexus, members delve into the world of coding and programming, learning languages like Python, Java, and C++. The club offers coding challenges, hackathons, and workshops on software development, helping members build a strong foundation in computer science. It’s a supportive community where coders of all levels come together to share knowledge, collaborate on projects, and stay updated with the latest technologies.

## Sports Mania

Sports Mania is where enthusiasts come to play, compete, and celebrate the joy of sports. From friendly matches to competitive tournaments, members engage in a variety of sports activities, including football, volleyball, and more. The club promotes physical fitness, teamwork, and sportsmanship, creating a lively and energetic atmosphere for sports lovers to connect and enjoy their favourite games.

## Cult-mosaic

Cult-mosaic celebrates diversity and cultural exchange through a variety of activities and events. The club aims to promote cultural awareness, understanding, and appreciation, fostering a sense of unity and harmony among members from diverse backgrounds.

## Finance Club

We explore investment strategies, financial markets, and wealth management. Join our vibrant community to gain valuable skills, insights, and experiences to empower students financial future.

## Marketing Club

Unlock the secrets of successful marketing with ‘MAntra’, the Marketing Club at Shree Devi Institute of Technology. Through workshops, competitions, and real-world projects, we empower students to become savvy marketers, equipped with the skills and knowledge to excel in today’s fast-paced business environment. Join us and let your creativity take flight!

## HR

Join ‘HRiday’, where passion meets purpose! At Shree Devi Institute of Technology, our HR Club is more than just a club; it’s a community dedicated to nurturing talent, fostering leadership, and shaping the future of HR professionals. Join us to explore the exciting world of human resources, gain practical skills, and unleash your full potential.

## Samarpan

Welcome to Samarpan, the heartbeat of social change at Shree Devi Institute of Technology! Join us in making a difference as we embark on a journey of compassion, empowerment, and community outreach. Together, let’s create a brighter, more inclusive tomorrow, one act of kindness at a time.

## Eco Club

Welcome to Sankalp, the Eco Club at Shree Devi Institute of Technology, where we are committed to making a green difference! Join us in our mission to create a sustainable future through conservation, awareness, and action. Let’s work together to protect our planet and inspire positive change in our community.

sections.heading: Overview
paragraphs: Dear Students, Faculty, Industry Partners, and Visitors,

Welcome to the Training and Placement Department of Shree Devi Institute of Technology (SDIT), where we are dedicated to empowering our students with the skills, knowledge, and opportunities they need to succeed in the professional world.

As the Training and Placement Officer, it is my privilege to lead a dynamic team committed to facilitating career readiness and enhancing employability among our students. Our mission is to bridge the gap between academia and industry by providing comprehensive training, career guidance, and placement assistance.

At SDIT, we recognize that academic excellence alone is not enough to thrive in today’s competitive job market. That’s why we offer a range of training programs, workshops, and seminars designed to enhance students’ technical competencies, soft skills, and professional demeanor. From technical certifications to mock interviews and resume building workshops, we provide students with the tools and resources they need to stand out to potential employers.

Our strong industry partnerships play a crucial role in our placement efforts. We collaborate closely with leading companies and organizations to facilitate internship opportunities, campus recruitment drives, and industry interactions. These partnerships not only provide students with valuable hands-on experience but also offer insights into industry trends and requirements.

Our placement record speaks volumes about the caliber of our students and the effectiveness of our training and placement initiatives. Year after year, our graduates secure placements in top-tier companies across various sectors, ranging from IT and engineering to finance and consulting.

Whether you are a student exploring internship opportunities, a recent graduate seeking employment, or an employer looking to recruit talented individuals, the Training and Placement section is here to assist you. We are committed to providing personalized guidance and support to help you achieve your career goals.

I encourage you to explore the Training and Placement section of our website to learn more about our programs, services, and upcoming placement activities. Together, let us embark on a journey of professional growth and success.
Thank you for choosing Shree Devi Institute of Technology as your partner in career development. We look forward to helping you realize your full potential and achieve your dreams.

Roshal Lynshal Nazareth
Training and Placement Officer, Shree Devi Institute of Technology.
